abstract:
Learning a skill is a complex cognitive task that requires processing multiple sensorimotor information. To support the skill learners, in this study, we explored and compared how to exploit AI wisely to teach skills. We selected engraving as the target skill and implemented it in a haptic-audio-visual (HAV) VR environment. As the haptic device, we used a desktop force-feedback device to render the movement and force profile of the tooltip. Starting from gathering experts’ motion and force profile data, we designed a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)-based AI model that discriminates the user's behavior and status of the tooltip using the acquired data. With the VR environment and the AI model, we evaluated four teaching strategies for haptic dexterous skill transfer–
                    Guidance, Disturbance, Hybrid
                    , and
                    Adaptive feedback
                    .
                    Guidance feedback
                    provides force cues to help the users, whereas
                    Disturbance
                    applies force that prevents the user's movement.
                    Hybrid
                    alters its mode between
                    Guidance
                    and
                    Disturbance
                    based on the user's performance. Lastly,
                    Adaptive feedback
                    modulates the threshold for altering the mode of
                    Hybrid
                    based on the user's history. We conducted a user experiment with seven sessions: one pre-test, three training sessions, one immediate retention, and two delayed retention sessions. In the results, we found: 1)
                    Guidance
                    showed a steep learning curve during the training sessions, but the participants lost the learning effect in the retention sessions, 2) the learning with
                    Hybrid
                    was the slowest but remained longer, even showed better performance in delayed retention tests, and 3)
                    Adaptive
                    strategy exhibited superior long-term learning effects compared to
                    Hybrid
                    and further suggested improved performance stability. These results seem to follow both the guidance hypothesis and the phenomenon of offline consolidation in learning, highlighting the importance of designing adaptive strategies in Teaching AI systems for dexterous skill learning.

ur.ai_reason: AI驱动的HCI技能学习，含用户评估
ur.tldr: 围绕雕刻技能在视听触觉VR环境中的迁移学习，基于专家运动与力数据训练LSTM模型识别用户行为与工具状态，实验比较Guidance、Disturbance、Hybrid与Adaptive feedback四种触觉辅助教学策略对学习成效的影响，探讨AI驱动自适应辅助的最优策略。

title: Towards An Optimal Strategy for Haptic Dexterous Skill Learning: Development of AI-Driven Adaptive Assistance
title_zh: 面向触觉灵巧技能学习的优化策略：AI驱动的自适应辅助开发
